meaning:
ὠφελέω, -ῶ
(ὄφελος), [in LXX chiefly for יָעַל hi. ;]
to help, benefit, do good, profit: absol., Rom.2:25; οὐδέν (do no good; see Field, Notes, 21), Mat.27:24, Jhn.6:63 12:19; with accusative of person(s), Heb.4:2; with dupl. accusative, Mrk.8:36, 1Co.14:6, Gal.5:2; pass., Heb.13:9; with accusative, Mat.15:5 16:26, Mrk.5:26 7:11, Luk.9:25, 1Co.13:3.†
(AS)

renderings.bsb: this is doing you no good

elsewhere.note: But you say, ‘Whoever may tell his father or his mother, “Whatever help you might otherwise have gotten from me is a gift devoted to God,”
and had suffered many things by many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was no better, but rather grew worse,
For what does it profit a man if he gains the whole world, and loses or forfeits his own self?
It is the spirit who gives life. The flesh profits nothing. The words that I speak to you are spirit, and are life.
For circumcision indeed profits, if you are a doer of the law, but if you are a transgressor of the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
If I give away all my goods to feed the poor, and if I give my body to be burned, but don’t have love, it profits me nothing.
Behold, I, Paul, tell you that if you receive circumcision, Christ will profit you nothing.
For indeed we have had good news preached to us, even as they also did, but the word they heard didn’t profit them, because it wasn’t mixed with faith by those…
